title: Both a bit off
setting: A weekday morning outside the apartment building. Satou-san is back from his morning walk and runs into Kenta, who is heading to work and doesn't look well.

speakers.name: Boss
speakers.voice: male, 50s, brisk but friendly, heard over the phone

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu, kenta-san. oya, guai ga warusou desu ne.
lines.ja: おはようございます、ケンタさん。おや、具合が悪そうですね。
lines.kana: おはようございます、けんたさん。おや、ぐあいがわるそうですね。
lines.english: Good morning, Kenta. Oh dear, you don't look well.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. kinou kara chotto guai ga warukute.
lines.ja: おはようございます。昨日からちょっと具合が悪くて。
lines.kana: おはようございます。きのうからちょっとぐあいがわるくて。
lines.english: Morning. I've been feeling a bit unwell since yesterday.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kibun ga warui n desu ka?
lines.kana: きぶんがわるいんですか？

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: iie, ima wa daijoubu desu. demo kinou, densha ga kondete, kibun ga waruku natchatte.
lines.ja: いいえ、今は大丈夫です。でも昨日、電車が混んでて、気分が悪くなっちゃって。
lines.kana: いいえ、いまはだいじょうぶです。でもきのう、でんしゃがこんでて、きぶんがわるくなっちゃって。
lines.english: No, I'm all right now. But yesterday the train was packed, and I started feeling sick.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: guai ga warui noni, oshigoto ni iku n desu ka?
lines.ja: 具合が悪いのに、お仕事に行くんですか？
lines.kana: ぐあいがわるいのに、おしごとにいくんですか？
lines.english: You're not well, and you're still going to work?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: hai. kyou wa yasumenai n desu yo.
lines.ja: はい。今日は休めないんですよ。
lines.kana: はい。きょうはやすめないんですよ。
lines.english: Yeah. I can't take today off.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: dame desu yo. densha ni nottara, mata kibun ga waruku narimasu yo.
lines.ja: だめですよ。電車に乗ったら、また気分が悪くなりますよ。
lines.kana: だめですよ。でんしゃにのったら、またきぶんがわるくなりますよ。
lines.english: Oh, you mustn't. If you get on the train, you'll start feeling sick again.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, kyou wa yasumimasu. are? sumaho no choushi warui naa.
lines.ja: じゃあ、今日は休みます。あれ？スマホの調子悪いなあ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、きょうはやすみます。あれ？すまほのちょうしわるいなあ。
lines.english: All right, I'll take the day off. Huh? My phone's acting up.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: oya oya. kenta-san mo sumaho mo, choushi ga warui n desu ne.
lines.ja: おやおや。ケンタさんもスマホも、調子が悪いんですね。
lines.kana: おやおや。けんたさんもすまほも、ちょうしがわるいんですね。
lines.english: Oh my. So you and your phone are both a bit off today.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: honto desu yo. kono sumaho, zutto choushi ga warui n desu.
lines.ja: ほんとですよ。このスマホ、ずっと調子が悪いんです。
lines.kana: ほんとですよ。このすまほ、ずっとちょうしがわるいんです。
lines.english: Tell me about it. This phone's been acting up for ages.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, ohayou gozaimasu. sumimasen, kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai.
lines.ja: もしもし、おはようございます。すみません、今日は体調が悪いので、休ませてください。
lines.kana: もしもし、おはようございます。すみません、きょうはたいちょうがわるいので、やすませてください。
lines.english: Hello, good morning. I'm sorry, I'm not feeling well today. Could I take the day off?

lines.speaker: boss
lines.romaji: taichou warui no? daijoubu? ii yo, kyou wa yasunde.
lines.ja: 体調悪いの？大丈夫？いいよ、今日は休んで。
lines.kana: たいちょうわるいの？だいじょうぶ？いいよ、きょうはやすんで。
lines.english: You're not feeling well? Are you okay? Sure, take the day off.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yokatta desu ne. taichou ga warukattara, yasumanai to dame desu yo.
lines.ja: よかったですね。体調が悪かったら、休まないとだめですよ。
lines.kana: よかったですね。たいちょうがわるかったら、やすまないとだめですよ。
lines.english: Good. When you're under the weather, you have to rest.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: satou-san wa, kyou mo sanpo desu ka?
lines.ja: 佐藤さんは、今日も散歩ですか？
lines.kana: さとうさんは、きょうもさんぽですか？
lines.english: Were you out on your walk again today, Satou-san?

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: ee. saikin, choushi ga ii n desu yo. mainichi sanpo ni itte imasu kara ne.
lines.ja: ええ。最近、調子がいいんですよ。毎日散歩に行っていますからね。
lines.kana: ええ。さいきん、ちょうしがいいんですよ。まいにちさんぽにいっていますからね。
lines.english: I was. I've been in good shape lately. I go for a walk every day, you see.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ii desu ne. boku mo choushi ga yoku nattara, sanpo ni ikou kana.
lines.ja: いいですね。僕も調子がよくなったら、散歩に行こうかな。
lines.kana: いいですね。ぼくもちょうしがよくなったら、さんぽにいこうかな。
lines.english: That's great. Maybe I'll start going for walks too, once I'm feeling better.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kenta-san mo sumaho mo, choushi ga yoku naru to ii desu ne.
lines.ja: ケンタさんもスマホも、調子がよくなるといいですね。
lines.kana: けんたさんもすまほも、ちょうしがよくなるといいですね。
lines.english: Here's hoping you and your phone are both back in shape soon.

choices.english: Kenta isn't well, but his boss says he can't have the day off, so he heads for the train.
Satou-san isn't well, so Kenta stays home from work to keep him company on his walk.
Kenta isn't well. Satou-san talks him out of going to work, and Kenta calls in sick on his glitchy phone.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta isn't well (guai ga warusou / guai ga warukute). In line 6 he says he can't take today off, but Satou-san warns him he'll feel sick on the train again (line 7), so he decides to stay home (line 8: kyou wa yasumimasu). His phone is acting up (lines 8-10), but the call goes through: he calls in sick (line 11) and his boss tells him to take the day off (line 12). A is wrong because the boss says ii yo, kyou wa yasunde (sure, take the day off). B is wrong because Satou-san is the one in good shape (line 15: saikin, choushi ga ii n desu yo). Kenta only says he might take up walks once he's better (line 16).

questions.english: Your friend Yuki asks, "ne, kyou karaoke ikanai?" (Hey, want to go to karaoke today?) You're not feeling great. Say sorry and tell her you're feeling a bit unwell.
questions.ja: ね、今日カラオケ行かない？
questions.kana: ね、きょうからおけいかない？
questions.answer: Turn her down with guai ga warui, softened with chotto: gomen, kyou wa chotto guai warui n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen, kyou wa chotto guai warui n da.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん、今日はちょっと具合悪いんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I'm not feeling too great today.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen ne, kinou kara chotto guai ga warukute.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめんね、昨日からちょっと具合が悪くて。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've been feeling a bit unwell since yesterday.

questions.explanation: Guai ga warui is the everyday 'I'm not feeling well'. Kenta uses it with Satou-san in line 2 (kinou kara chotto guai ga warukute), and Satou-san sees it on his face in line 1 (guai ga warusou). Chotto softens it, and with a friend ga often drops (guai warui). The n da gives your reason for saying no. Byouki desu would sound like you have an actual illness. Taichou ga warui also works, but it's the more careful word you'd keep for work.

questions.english: It's a workday morning and you feel unwell. You phone your manager, Tanaka-san, and he picks up: "hai, tanaka desu. ohayou gozaimasu." (Hello, Tanaka speaking. Good morning.) Tell him you're not feeling well and ask for the day off.
questions.ja: はい、田中です。おはようございます。
questions.kana: はい、たなかです。おはようございます。
questions.answer: Use the work-safe taichou ga warui and ask for the day off: sumimasen, kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai.

modelAnswers.romaji: ohayou gozaimasu. sumimasen, kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: おはようございます。すみません、今日は体調が悪いので、休ませてください。
modelAnswers.english: Good morning. I'm sorry, I'm not feeling well today. Could I take the day off?

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, kinou kara chotto taichou ga warui n desu. kyou wa yasunde mo ii desu ka?
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、昨日からちょっと体調が悪いんです。今日は休んでもいいですか？
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, I've been a bit under the weather since yesterday. Would it be all right if I took today off?

questions.explanation: At work, taichou ga warui is the safe phrase for calling in sick. Kenta tells his neighbour guai ga warui (line 2), but on the phone to his boss he switches to taichou ga warui (line 11: kyou wa taichou ga warui node, yasumasete kudasai), and his boss repeats it back (line 12). Node gives the reason politely. Yasumasete kudasai asks to be let off, and yasunde mo ii desu ka asks permission. Guai ga warui would be understood, but taichou is the careful word for your manager.

questions.english: After deciding to stay home, Kenta takes out his phone and frowns at it. What does he say?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、スマホを見て、何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、すまほをみて、なんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, sumaho o mite, nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: Line 8: sumaho no choushi warui naa. Choushi ga warui is for a device that still works, just badly. A is what English 'my phone's broken' turns into, but kowareta means it broke and has stopped working. Kenta's phone still works: he makes his call on it in line 11, and he says it's been acting up for ages (line 10: zutto choushi ga warui n desu). C is the opposite, choushi ga ii (working well). That doesn't fit his puzzled 'are?' or Satou-san's joke in line 9 that Kenta and his phone are both off (kenta-san mo sumaho mo, choushi ga warui n desu ne).

questions.english: When Kenta asks about his walk, Satou-san says "saikin, choushi ga ii n desu yo." What does he mean?
questions.ja: 佐藤さんは、最近どうですか？
questions.kana: さとうさんは、さいきんどうですか？
questions.romaji: satou-san wa, saikin dou desu ka?

choices.english: He's been in good shape lately, thanks to his daily walks.
He's in a good mood this morning because the weather is nice.
His phone has been working well lately, unlike Kenta's.

questions.explanation: Line 15: said about yourself, choushi ga ii means you're in good shape. Satou-san gives the reason straight away: mainichi sanpo ni itte imasu kara (I go for a walk every day). Kenta picks it up in line 16: choushi ga yoku nattara (once I'm feeling better). B is a mood, which would be kigen ga ii or kibun ga ii, and nobody mentions the weather. C: choushi does work for devices (Kenta's sumaho no choushi warui, line 8), but Satou-san says nothing about a phone. He's talking about himself and his walks.

questions.english: You and Mai are squeezed onto a packed train, and you start to feel sick. Mai asks, "densha, sugoku konderu ne. daijoubu?" (The train's so packed. You okay?) Tell her you're feeling a bit sick.
questions.ja: 電車、すごく混んでるね。大丈夫？
questions.kana: でんしゃ、すごくこんでるね。だいじょうぶ？
questions.answer: Say no, you feel sick, with kibun ga warui: uun, chotto kibun ga warui.

modelAnswers.ja: ううん、ちょっと気分が悪い。
modelAnswers.english: No, I feel a bit sick.

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, chotto kibun ga waruku natte kita.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、ちょっと気分が悪くなってきた。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm starting to feel a bit sick.

questions.explanation: Kibun ga warui is feeling sick or faint right now, in a crowd or a stuffy train. That's what happened to Kenta yesterday (line 4: densha ga kondete, kibun ga waruku natchatte), and Satou-san warns it will happen again (line 7). Waruku natte kita says it's coming on. It isn't English 'I feel bad', which is guilt (warui na). Guai ga warui is general unwellness, not this sudden 'I'm going to be sick' feeling.

newWords.english: take time off; rest (yasumenai = can't take off; yasumasete kudasai = please let me have the day off)
get crowded (densha ga kondete = the train was packed)
oh my, oh dear (an older speaker's mild surprise; oya oya)
